timeline_reviews.summary: Serial CLI stream contains transport events only; semantic actions are projected from the Claude project trajectory.
Serial parent trajectory: directly implements the Rust project, writes modules and tests, builds, verifies byte output, and returns final summary.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the black-box Rust 2021 port, std-only constraint, Cargo/project layout, test5.rs entry, and reference output 1; the workflow context expanded the task into a broad general-purpose Clipper2-compatible clipping engine design.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent validated the environment, created task reminders for design, implementation, entry file, and verification, but marked only design in progress and delegated a multi-phase design workflow before implementation.
parallel.implementation: Only /output/src and /output/Cargo.toml were created by the parent; no Rust source modules, test5.rs entry file, compiled binary, or tests were produced before timeout.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The workflow was supposed to synthesize a SPEC.md for later implementation, but it returned null/killed; artifact validation found only Cargo.toml and expected test5.rs was absent.
parallel.verification: Parallel checked rustc/cargo versions, experimented with layout compatibility, and ran the reference C++ binary, but never built or tested a Rust solution.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The process ended with returncode 143 after about 2399 seconds; official evaluation completed and failed 0/1 because the required implementation artifact was missing.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same prompt requirements, confirmed the C++ binary prints 1 with or without arguments, saw no Clipper source, and kept the implementation std-only.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked as a single owner without delegation: directly implemented the project, then added tests, built artifacts, and prepared the final response.
serial.implementation: Wrote Cargo.toml, clipper2 module files, core types, engine, facade functions, root test5.rs, library target, and regression tests for the boolean operations.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Built the release Cargo binary and standalone rustc binary, delivered /output/test5.rs plus /output/test5 and target/release/test5, and final status artifact validation was ok.
serial.verification: Ran the C++ reference, a custom verification harness, cargo test with 10 tests, cargo build, rustc build, and byte-for-byte comparisons over five argument sets.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved required behavior is visible at closure; the final note flagged interpretation of the executable path wording, but the official evaluator passed 1/1.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel read the task and reference behavior, then encoded a broad design context requiring a general-purpose clipping engine before code.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial read the same prompt, confirmed reference output and ignored argv, and implemented the required Rust project directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both understood the core requirements, but parallel converted them into a design prerequisite that blocked delivery; serial translated them into concrete source and executable artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into a workflow with four design agents, judge agents, and synthesize, while parent task reminders for implementation and verification remained behind design.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept ownership local and proceeded from exploration to implementation, tests, builds, and final delivery without child agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel allocated active work to design/review rather than the required implementation path; serial kept the implementation path continuously owned and executed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were design-only and told children not to write files; retries restarted from the same broad context without inherited checkpoints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent handoff; the same actor carried task context into source writes, tests, and final build decisions.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced context handoff and retry boundaries that failed to return a usable spec; serial avoided those boundaries by keeping context in one trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created only project scaffolding and Cargo.toml, with no test5.rs or library implementation in the final artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the entry file, module tree, engine, facade, tests, and then compiled the outputs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete implementation gap is total: serial produced the required codebase while parallel stopped after setup.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched a background workflow, polled for SPEC.md, saw no spec, and ended with the workflow killed and result null.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial inspected each local build/test result immediately and used those results to continue to final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel never received or joined the planned design result; serial kept all intermediate results in the main line and acted on them.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had no completed implementation pieces to integrate; artifact validation showed only Cargo.toml and missing test5.rs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial assembled a coherent final tree with Cargo.lock, test5.rs, src modules, tests, and compiled binaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no write collision, but serial achieved final-tree assembly while parallel had only an incomplete scaffold.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified the reference binary and layout but performed no Rust build/test/evaluator-aligned local acceptance before closure; official evaluation failed 0/1.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran cargo tests, built both Cargo and rustc binaries, compared stdout byte-for-byte, and official evaluation passed 1/1.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had end-to-end acceptance evidence for the delivered Rust program; parallel had only preparatory checks and no program to verify.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed about the full 2400-second cell budget, had 23 subagents/workflow children, and process_ok was false after timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 1256 seconds with process_ok true and more than 1100 seconds remaining in the provider retry budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel budget was spent before implementation could be delivered, while serial closed normally with verified artifacts.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records make this a serial_only_pass pair: parallel failed 0/1 while serial passed 1/1. The difference is not evaluator drift; it is delivery. Parallel spent the run on a design workflow and retry loop, produced only Cargo.toml, had an empty final response, and missed the required test5.rs. Serial directly wrote, tested, built, and delivered the Rust project, including test5.rs and compiled binaries.
parallel_contributors: Parent gated implementation on a design workflow and waited for SPEC.md instead of implementing concurrently.
The workflow restarted stalled design children without checkpoints and was killed with no final spec/result.
The final artifact lacked /output/test5.rs and all Rust implementation modules.
serial_contributors: Serial directly implemented the Rust project in the main trajectory without delegation overhead.
Serial built and tested the implementation, including 10 cargo tests and byte-exact comparisons against the C++ binary.
Serial artifact validation found the expected entry file, source modules, tests, and binaries.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The substantive code difference is absence versus presence of an implementation; no separate ordinary coding defect is needed to explain the official outcome.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The parent created an implementation task and retained implicit ownership, but blocked it behind the design workflow; the absence of code is a gated/timeout consequence, not an ownerless work split.
No completed component implementations existed that required an integration owner; the run never reached multiple implementation components.
No complete packageable component set existed for final assembly; the required entry file was missing because implementation did not happen.
The parent made an explicit task pipeline for design, implementation, entry file, and verification; the pipeline stalled behind design rather than lacking an owner.

The parent used the design workflow as a mandatory preflight: the script defines design, judge, and synthesize before returning a spec, the parent launched it and then only waited/polled while implementation did not begin. This satisfies the gate definition because productive implementation was delayed behind a prerequisite analysis artifact and the parallel artifact lacked test5.rs.
candidates.realized_consequence: Implementation remained deferred behind the design spec; the delivered artifact contained only Cargo.toml and missed the required /output/test5.rs entry file.
candidates.near_match_reason: The design work did not complete as a separate investigation phase that then left late implementation; the observable failure was the parent-imposed preflight gate itself.

candidates.reason: The design/investigation stage never completed and handed back usable findings before implementation; the retained gate label is the specific parent boundary.
Implementation capacity was displaced, but the more specific parent preflight gate and checkpoint-free retry boundaries explain the same chain.
The workflow spent the budget across fan-out and retries, but the retained Checkpoint-Free Retry captures the directly evidenced repeated same-scope replacement episode.
No single child was assigned one overbroad implementation scope; children were design/judge/synthesis workers and the observed problem was repeated stalled retries.
The design children received the task/environment/acceptance context for their design-only assignment; implementation was excluded by plan, not accidentally omitted from a child brief.
No separately owned implementation components were delegated, so there was no cross-agent code interface contract to omit or reconcile.
No known finding disappeared in transfer; repeated children were given fresh full prompts and failed before producing reusable findings.
Some judge outputs were long, but no parent-visible decision failed because an available handoff was too bulky to consume.
No receiver acted on superseded workspace or requirement state; the workspace largely stayed at only Cargo.toml.
Judge outputs differed about the empty candidate set, but no unadjudicated conflict was integrated into a wrong implementation or final decision.
The parallel parent did not present the whole task as complete; final.txt is empty and the process ended by timeout.

The workflow repeatedly replaced stalled design agents with fresh agents for the same keys, while each fresh child restarted from the same design-only prompt and basic task probing rather than inheriting a partial checkpoint or narrowed next milestone. This consumed the workflow window and left the parent without a returned spec.
candidates.realized_consequence: The workflow produced no usable design/spec return after repeated same-scope restarts, exhausting the decision window before any implementable guidance reached the parent.
candidates.near_match_reason: The broad fan-out budget symptom is real, but the directly evidenced, more specific boundary is the retry of same-scope design work without inherited checkpoints.

The parent was killed while waiting and did not receive a clean child failure with remaining time; the actionable boundary is the preflight/retry design chain, not a later takeover failure.
No completed implementation or final workflow result was available to the parent and then ignored; judge outputs were internal to the workflow.
The parent did wait and poll for SPEC.md, but it also attempted a journal check; the direct cause is the mandatory gate and checkpoint-free workflow retries, not an independent missed-progress wait.
No concurrent implementation paths produced competing code or build ownership; children were design-only or judge/synthesis workers.
There is no evidence of two live agents editing the same source/configuration file.
No source file produced by one actor was replaced by another; the only durable source-like write was Cargo.toml by the parent.
No required executable or entry-point source existed for another actor to overwrite.
No broad cleanup or promotion replaced a current final tree.
The workflow children were instructed not to write files and no shared-workspace provenance instability is shown.
No generated artifact, cache, fixture, or temporary output from one actor was consumed by another as stable input.
